28	
29	Three artifacts ship in this task:
30	
31	1. **`runtime/abi/src/types.ts`** — TypeScript surfaces:
32	   - `ExecutorInput` — the structured input the orchestrator passes to
33	     an executor. Fields per technical-design §4.2: `taskId`,
34	     `featureId`, `workspaceId`, `taskRepoUrl`, `taskRepoBranch`,
35	     `taskRepoPath`, `briefingPath`, `resultPath`, `budgetTokens?`,
36	     `sshKeyPath`, `githubToken`. Note: no `mgmtRepoPath` — the
37	     executor never reads or writes the management repo (per D5).

39	     `taskRepoPath` from `taskRepoUrl` on `taskRepoBranch` (clone if
40	     absent, fetch + checkout + pull if present and origin matches).
41	   - `ExecutorResult` — the structured output the executor produces
42	     via `result.json`. Fields: `terminal_status`
43	     (`"in_review" | "blocked" | "failed"`), `token_usage?`,
44	     `blocked_reason?` (required when `terminal_status === "blocked"`),
45	     `blocked_suggestion?` (required when `terminal_status === "blocked"`).

323	## T6 — PR ownership split (revised D5) + termination safety — executor owns impl PR; post-hoc recovery on abnormal exit
324	
325	### Description
326	
327	Added 2026-05-02 after T4's handoff drafting revealed that the original
328	D5 ("orchestrator opens the PR; runtimes never call `pr-create`") was
329	silently violated by the implementation: the Claude executor opens the
330	impl PR via the `pr-create` skill (with rich PR body and test plan),
331	and the orchestrator's `openImplPr` is reduced to an idempotent no-op
332	that finds and reuses the existing PR. This task formalizes the
333	revised D5 — executor owns the implementation PR, orchestrator owns
334	the management/workspace PR — and adds `pr_url` to the ABI so the
335	orchestrator can record the executor-opened PR in the task YAML.
336	
337	The orchestrator does **not** gate on test outcomes, and PR opening
338	itself is **not** gated on implementation outcome. Per D4, the
339	orchestrator is pure workflow-state code; the executor's internal
340	quality gate (tests, lint, etc.) is private to the executor. The impl
341	PR is part of the task lifecycle (same model as the workspace PR
342	opened at claim time) — opened whenever there are commits to PR,
343	regardless of whether tests passed. Test failure means
344	`terminal_status: "blocked"` with `blocked_reason: "tests_failed"`
345	**and** the PR is still opened (as draft, or with a failure-summary
346	comment) so the failed attempt is documented. `pr_url` is reported
347	across all terminal_status values whenever a PR exists.
348	
349	The revised D5 is documented in `product-spec.md` D5 (revised
350	2026-05-02) and `technical-design.md` §4.6.1.
351	
352	**Scope expanded 2026-05-02 to include termination safety.** Claude's
353	`--max-turns` cap (and any other abnormal exit — signal, crash,
354	timeout) currently leaves no record: no committed work, no draft PR,
355	no handover. This violates the lifecycle invariant from revised D5
356	(impl PR exists for any task with commits). T6 now also implements
357	the two-layer termination safety mechanism documented in
358	`technical-design.md` §4.6.2:
359	
360	- **Layer 1** (always-on, deterministic): an executor-side post-hoc
361	  recovery routine runs in `try/finally` around the Claude spawn.
362	  Commits any uncommitted work as `wip(<task_id>): incomplete`,
363	  pushes, opens a draft impl PR if none exists, writes a stub
364	  `handover.md`, and produces a valid `result.json` regardless of
365	  how the spawn ended.
366	- **Layer 2** (best-effort, briefing-encoded): the briefing template
367	  instructs Claude to commit/push after each substantial action and
368	  to perform a graceful checkpoint (open draft PR, write rich
369	  handover.md, exit cleanly with `terminal_status: "blocked"`,
370	  `blocked_reason: "handover_for_continuation"`) when it senses the
371	  budget is running out.
372	- **Layer 3** (orchestrator surface): when an agent re-claims a task
373	  with an existing draft PR, the briefing generator reads
374	  `handover.md` from the impl repo branch and prepends it to the
375	  new agent's briefing.
376	
377	Scope (revised D5):
378	- Add `pr_url` (string) field to the `result.json` schema
379	  (`runtime/abi/src/types.ts` and `schema.ts`). Reported whenever the
380	  executor opened an impl PR — independent of `terminal_status`.
381	- Update the Claude executor (`runtime/executors/claude/src/index.ts`)
382	  to:
383	  - Always invoke the impl-PR-open path whenever there are commits on
384	    the feature branch — regardless of whether tests passed. The PR
385	    is part of the task lifecycle, not an artifact of test outcome.
386	  - Extract the PR URL from Claude's stdout (the `pr-create` skill
387	    reports the PR URL it opens) and populate `result.json.pr_url`
388	    whenever a PR was opened.
389	  - When Claude's test plan reports failures, write
390	    `terminal_status: "blocked"` with `blocked_reason: "tests_failed"`
391	    AND `pr_url` (the PR documents the failed attempt — possibly as
392	    draft or with a failure-summary comment).
393	- Update orchestrator dispatch (`runtime/orchestrator/src/side-effects/dispatch.ts`):
394	  - Remove the call to `openImplPr`.
395	  - Whenever `result.pr_url` is present, pass it to `mutateTaskYaml`
396	    to record in the task YAML's `pr.url` field — regardless of
397	    `terminal_status`. A blocked task with a draft PR still records
398	    its `pr_url`.
399	  - No new gating logic — `terminal_status` translation paths
400	    (in_review / blocked / failed) are unchanged.
401	- Delete `runtime/orchestrator/src/side-effects/open-pr.ts` and remove
402	  its imports.
403	- Update `runtime/abi/docs/abi-spec.md` to document the revised D5,
404	  the new `pr_url` field, and the executor's PR-open responsibility.
405	- Update `runtime/executors/claude/src/CLAUDE.md` (or equivalent
406	  briefing template) to make the impl-PR-open step an explicit
407	  executor responsibility, applied regardless of test outcome.
408	
409	Scope (termination safety — added 2026-05-02):
410	- Add `handover_path` (string, optional) field to the `result.json`
411	  schema. Path to a `handover.md` file written by either the
412	  executor (Layer 2) or the post-hoc recovery routine (Layer 1).
413	- Implement Layer 1 — executor-side post-hoc recovery in a new
414	  `runtime/executors/claude/src/recovery.ts`. The recovery routine
415	  is invoked from a `try/finally` around the Claude spawn in
416	  `index.ts`. It commits any uncommitted work as
417	  `wip(<task_id>): incomplete — agent terminated unexpectedly`,
418	  pushes the branch, opens a draft impl PR if none exists, writes a
419	  stub `handover.md`, and produces a valid `result.json` with
420	  `terminal_status: "blocked"` + appropriate `blocked_reason` +
421	  `pr_url` + `handover_path`.
422	- The recovery is **idempotent** — if the agent already wrote a
423	  valid `result.json` with `terminal_status: "in_review"`, the
424	  recovery validates and exits without rewriting. If the agent
425	  already opened a non-draft PR, the recovery does not re-draft it.
426	- The recovery **must not throw** — each step is individually
427	  wrapped in try/catch. The `finally` block always produces a
428	  `result.json`.
429	- Implement Layer 2 — the briefing template in
430	  `runtime/orchestrator/src/briefing/` includes a "checkpoint
431	  discipline" section (see `technical-design.md` §4.6.2 for the
432	  exact text) instructing Claude to commit/push after each
433	  substantial action and to perform a graceful checkpoint when the
434	  budget is running out.
435	- Implement Layer 3 — `runtime/orchestrator/src/briefing/agent-context.ts`
436	  reads `handover.md` from the task working directory if present
437	  and prepends it to the new agent's briefing on re-claim.
438	
439	Out of scope (unchanged):
440	- Removing `pr-create` skill from Claude's loaded skills — it is the

## T1 — Define runtime ABI — types, schema, fake-executor fixture

### Description

Establish `workflow/runtime/abi/` as a self-contained package that
defines the contract every executor must satisfy. T1 produces no
behavior change to the live runtime; it adds a new package alongside
the legacy `workflow/agent-runtime/` and exposes the types that T2
will wire against.

Three artifacts ship in this task:

1. **`runtime/abi/src/types.ts`** — TypeScript surfaces:
   - `ExecutorInput` — the structured input the orchestrator passes to
     an executor. Fields per technical-design §4.2: `taskId`,
     `featureId`, `workspaceId`, `taskRepoUrl`, `taskRepoBranch`,
     `taskRepoPath`, `briefingPath`, `resultPath`, `budgetTokens?`,
     `sshKeyPath`, `githubToken`. Note: no `mgmtRepoPath` — the
     executor never reads or writes the management repo (per D5).
     The executor is responsible for materializing the repo at
     `taskRepoPath` from `taskRepoUrl` on `taskRepoBranch` (clone if
     absent, fetch + checkout + pull if present and origin matches).
   - `ExecutorResult` — the structured output the executor produces
     via `result.json`. Fields: `terminal_status`
     (`"in_review" | "blocked" | "failed"`), `token_usage?`,
     `blocked_reason?` (required when `terminal_status === "blocked"`),
     `blocked_suggestion?` (required when `terminal_status === "blocked"`).
   - `ExecutorAdapter` — the orchestrator-side seam:
     `run(input: ExecutorInput): Promise<ExecutorResult>`.

2. **`runtime/abi/src/schema.ts`** — JSON Schema for `result.json`,
   used by orchestrator to validate executor output on read. Schema
   violations are mapped to `terminal_status: "failed",
   blocked_reason: "result_schema_invalid"`.

3. **`runtime/abi/src/fake-executor.ts`** — `FakeAdapter`
   implementation of `ExecutorAdapter`. Returns a configurable
   `ExecutorResult` synchronously; never spawns anything; used by
   orchestrator tests in T3.

4. **`runtime/abi/docs/abi-spec.md`** — skeleton spec document for
   third-party runtime authors. Skeleton only — full content lands in
   T4. T1 ships the structure and links to the type definitions.

This is the foundation. Wave 1, no upstream blockers.

### Required skills

- typescript-best-practices

### Subtasks

- [ ] Create `workflow/runtime/abi/` directory with `package.json` and `tsconfig.json`
- [ ] Define `ExecutorInput`, `ExecutorResult`, `TerminalStatus`, `ExecutorAdapter` in `src/types.ts`
- [ ] Define JSON Schema for `result.json` in `src/schema.ts`; export a validator function
- [ ] Implement `FakeAdapter` in `src/fake-executor.ts`: factory takes a configurable result, returns an adapter; no I/O
- [ ] Create `docs/abi-spec.md` skeleton with section headings (Inputs, Outputs, Side effects executor performs, Side effects executor never performs, Lifecycle); leave full content for T4
- [ ] Add unit tests for the JSON Schema validator: valid in_review, valid blocked with reason+suggestion, invalid (missing reason on blocked), invalid (unknown terminal_status)
- [ ] Verify the package builds in isolation (`yarn build` or equivalent inside `runtime/abi/`)
- [ ] Verify nothing imports from `runtime/abi/` yet — this package is intentionally orphaned at end of T1

## T2 — Big-bang split — extract orchestrator + Claude executor, cutover

### Description

The cutover PR. Per technical-design §4 and §6, T2 is one PR that:

- Creates `workflow/runtime/orchestrator/` and moves the polling loop,
  claim, poll, eligibility, bootstrap, and briefing-generation code
  into it. Most of the diff is git-detected file renames + import-path
  updates.
- Creates `workflow/runtime/executors/claude/` and moves the body of
  `agent-runtime/src/loop/run-claude.ts` into it as the ABI-conformant
  entrypoint: reads env vars per `ExecutorInput`, runs `claude -p`,
  writes `result.json` per `ExecutorResult`, exits 0/non-zero.
- Implements `SubProcessAdapter` (TD-A2) in
  `runtime/orchestrator/src/adapter/spawn.ts`: spawns the Claude
  executor binary as a child process inside the same container,
  serializes `ExecutorInput` into env vars, waits for exit, reads and
  validates `result.json`.
- **Moves workflow side effects** from inside-Claude responsibility to
  orchestrator code (`runtime/orchestrator/src/side-effects/`):
  PR open, task YAML mutation (`in_progress → in_review/blocked`),
  dependency unblock (auto-ready rule), log entries, branch sync.
  Today these are partly performed by Claude via `pr-create` skill +
  CLAUDE.md guidance; after T2 they are deterministic orchestrator
  code triggered by reading `result.json`.
- Updates the briefing-generation logic so the briefing markdown
  carries task-specific context only — workflow rules stop being
  injected into Claude's runtime context.
- Replaces the single bundled Dockerfile with two Dockerfiles:
  `runtime/orchestrator/Dockerfile` (lean — Node + git + GH token) and
  `runtime/executors/claude/Dockerfile` (Node + Claude CLI + task
  toolchains). On day 1 the deployed image can still bake both
  binaries together; the choice is per-deployment.
- Updates `docker-compose` template to point at new images.
- **Deletes** `workflow/agent-runtime/` entirely, including K8s
  CronJob and GH Actions templates (they would otherwise orphan
  pointing at removed paths — re-introduction is a follow-on
  feature).

package with fresh eyes and populate the concrete refactor checklist
under T5's `### Subtasks` section. T5's scope cannot be enumerated
until the split lands; T2's last act is to enumerate it.

T2 does **not** include orchestrator-internal refactors — those defer
to T5. T2 also does not include test rewrites — those defer to T3
(though existing tests must be migrated to the new layout and
continue to pass).

### Description

T6's briefing rewrite replaced the `/start-implementation` skill invocation with
inline steps, silently dropping three things the skill provided:

1. **Write unit tests** — the skill's Step 1 (implement) implies tests; the inline
   briefing said only "implement all required changes".
2. **Test-plan execution from `tasks.md`** — the skill's Step 3 reads the test plan
   from `tasks.md` and executes each item; the inline briefing said only "run the
   project's test suite".
3. **Post test-plan results as PR comment** — the skill's Step 4 posts results after
   PR creation; the inline briefing omitted this entirely (partially restored via a
   separate commit, but incorrectly placed inline).

spawns — the hook was not removed. The problem is that the briefing no longer tells
Claude to invoke `/start-implementation`, so the skill goes unused.

**Root cause:** T6 treated the skill as a human-only artifact and duplicated its
logic inline. The correct fix is to restore the skill invocation and make the
skill aware of the agent-runtime context so it behaves correctly in both settings.

**Design — `CLAUDE_AGENT_RUNTIME` guard pattern:**

When `printenv CLAUDE_AGENT_RUNTIME` returns `1`, the executor is running inside
the agent runtime. Two skills need guards:

- **`start-implementation`**: management-repo side effects (writing task YAML status,
  log entries) are skipped — the orchestrator owns those from `result.json`. The
  skill still: implements, writes tests, runs the test plan, creates the impl PR,
  posts the test-plan comment, and writes `result.json` to `$RESULT_PATH`.
- **`pr-create`**: task YAML updates (PR metadata, log entry, status → in_review)
  are skipped — the orchestrator handles these. The skill still: pushes the branch
  and creates the GitHub PR. Returns the PR URL.

  `printenv CLAUDE_AGENT_RUNTIME`. If `1`, apply the agent-runtime variant of each
  step (described below). If empty, existing behaviour is unchanged.
- **Agent-runtime Step 3 (test plan)**: when tests fail and cannot be fixed after
  3 attempts, do NOT hard-stop before opening a PR. Instead: continue to Step 4,
  open the PR as a draft, then write `result.json` with
  `terminal_status: "blocked"`, `blocked_reason: "tests_failed"`, and `pr_url`.

- **Agent-runtime Step 4 (create PR)**: invoke `/pr-create` as normal to open the

# Product Specification

## Feature
- Feature ID: `agent-runtime-split`
- Title: Split agent runtime into orchestration and execution layers

## Problem

Today the agent runtime (`workflow/agent-runtime/`, ~6.7k LOC) is a single Node.js
process that interleaves two very different responsibilities in one event loop:

1. **Orchestration** — discovering eligible tasks across watched workspaces,
   pulling repos, claiming tasks via the git-SHA protocol, polling GitHub for
   PR merges/conflicts, advancing task YAML state, opening and merging
   workspace PRs, enforcing dependency unblocks, writing audit logs.

2. **Execution** — generating a per-task agent briefing, spawning the
   `claude -p` subprocess inside the same container, capturing stdout, parsing
   token usage, and persisting the resulting task YAML mutations.

Concrete entanglement points:

- `agent-runtime/src/main.ts` owns the polling loop **and** dispatches Claude
  invocations from the same scope (imports `runAgentLoop`,
  `pullWorkspaces`, `checkInReviewPrs`, `handleMergeConflicts` side-by-side).
- `loop/run-claude.ts` requires `workspaceRoot`, `taskRepoRoot`, and
  `agentContext` — all orchestration-discovered state — to run.
- Token-budget enforcement straddles both layers: orchestration reads
  `budget.max_tokens_per_task` during eligibility, execution audits it
  post-exit.
- The runtime is hard-coded to `claude` as a binary. There is no abstraction
  point at which a different executor (e.g. Hermes / NousResearch) can be
  plugged in. The `agent-runtime-selector` feature already declared a
  task-level `execution.runtime: claude-code | hermes` field, but the runtime
  has nowhere to dispatch on it.

This coupling causes four concrete pains documented in the prior agent-runtime
features:

- **Cannot swap or mix executors.** Every task pays Claude API cost regardless
  of complexity (`agent-runtime-selector/product-spec.md`: "Many tasks in the
  workflow are routine and mechanical … where a cheaper or free runtime would
  produce equally good output.")
- **Cannot scale orchestration independently.** One container == one polling
  loop == one executor. Running N agents means running N copies of the
  orchestration loop, each independently polling GitHub and re-discovering

name: pr-create
description: Create PR from current task branch and update task PR metadata, using shared environment resolution.
---

## Environment

### Required (resolved via `resolve-project-env`)
| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `GITHUB_ACCOUNT` | GitHub username or org; used to construct PR target and remote URL |

---

## Must resolve environment first

Before any git push or PR operation, invoke:

- `resolve-project-env`

Required outputs:

- validated `project_root`
- resolved `SSH_KEY_PATH`
- resolved git identity values
- resolved `GITHUB_ACCOUNT`

If required values are missing, require the user to provide them. Do not guess.

## Git / SSH rule

When repo access requires SSH:

- use the SSH key resolved from project `.env` via `SSH_KEY_PATH`
- do not assume the default SSH key is correct

## GitHub API rule

Do NOT use the `gh` CLI to create pull requests. Use the GitHub REST API via `curl` instead. This avoids requiring `gh` to be installed on the host or in agent containers.

Use `GITHUB_TOKEN` from the project `.env` for authentication. If `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not set, fall back to reading `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` for the `oauth_token` under `github.com`.

Example:
```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls \
  -d '{"title":"...","body":"...","head":"<branch>","base":"<base_branch>"}'
```

## Must

- push branch if needed
- resolve the base branch from `workspace.yaml -> repos[].base_branch` for the task's repo (required; unset is an error)
- create PR against that explicit base branch using the GitHub REST API (not `gh` CLI)
- update task PR metadata
- append task log entry
- avoid duplicate PR creation

name: start-implementation
description: Safely begin implementation of a task stored as a single YAML task file, using shared environment resolution.
---

## Environment

### Required (resolved via `resolve-project-env`)
| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `SSH_KEY_PATH` | SSH private key for git clone/fetch/push |
| `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME` | Actor recorded in task log |
| `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL` | Actor recorded in task log |
| `<REPO_ID_UPPER>_LOCAL_PATH` | Local path to each repo used by tasks in this workspace |

---

## Must resolve environment first

Before any git or repo operation, invoke:

- `resolve-project-env`

Required outputs:

- validated `project_root`
- resolved `SSH_KEY_PATH`
- resolved git identity values
- resolved repo local path values

If required values are missing, require the user to provide them. Do not guess.

## Must verify

- task file exists
- task status is `ready` — **hard stop** if status is anything else (including `todo`, `in_progress`, `blocked`). Print the current status and stop. Do not proceed.
- all tasks in `depends_on` are `done`
- repo matches `workspace.yaml -> repos[].id`
- repo local path resolves correctly
- working tree is clean

## Git / SSH rule

When repo access requires SSH:

- use the SSH key resolved from project `.env` via `SSH_KEY_PATH`
- do not assume the default SSH key is correct

## Must then

Resolve the base branch from `workspace.yaml -> repos[].base_branch` for the task's repo (required; unset is an error).

### Implementation repo

1. **Fetch from remote** — never skip this; a stale local branch is not acceptable:
   ```
   git fetch origin
   ```

2. **Checkout and hard-reset to the remote base branch** — this is the only safe starting point:
   ```
   git checkout <base_branch>
   git reset --hard origin/<base_branch>
   ```
   **Hard stop** if either command fails — set `status: blocked`, set `blocked_reason` to the git error message, append a log entry, and stop.

3. **Create the feature branch**:
   ```
   git checkout -b feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   ```
   **Hard stop** if this fails — set `status: blocked`, set `blocked_reason` to the git error message, append a log entry, and stop.

   If the feature branch already exists locally (e.g. from a previous aborted attempt), delete it first:
   ```
   git branch -D feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   ```
   then repeat steps 2–3.

### Management repo

The task branch already exists on the management repo — `claimTask` created and pushed it as part of the claim. Do **not** create it again.

1. **Fetch from remote**:
   ```
   git fetch origin
   ```
   **Hard stop** if this fails — set `status: blocked`, append a log entry, and stop.

2. **Checkout and hard-reset to the existing task branch**:
   ```
   git checkout feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   git reset --hard origin/feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   ```
   **Hard stop** if either command fails (e.g. branch unexpectedly missing on remote) — set `status: blocked`, append a log entry, and stop. Do not proceed.

## Must append task log

- action: started
- actor: resolved `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`
- timestamp: real local time via `date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z` — never hardcode

### Task log entry format

Every log entry produced during an agent work phase must follow this schema:

```yaml
log:
  - action: started            # or work_phase_complete, blocked, etc.
    by: <GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL>
    at: <ISO 8601 timestamp>
    note: <optional free-text note>
    tokens:
      input: 0                 # input tokens used in this work phase (0 at start, filled at completion)
      output: 0                # output tokens generated
      total: 0                 # input + output
      cost_usd: 0.000          # estimated USD cost at current model rates
```

Update `tokens` in the completion log entry once the work phase ends. If token usage is unavailable, set all token values to `0` rather than omitting the field.

> **Do NOT write `rag_context_injected` or `rag_summary` on agent-produced log entries.** The runtime is the authoritative writer of those fields — it appends a separate `action: rag_pre_flight` entry to the task YAML before spawning you, and audits that entry on exit. Mutating, removing, or duplicating that entry causes the run to be force-blocked with `runtime_error`.

---

## RAG context — runtime-injected

Before this skill starts, the runtime has already:

1. Queried the RAG server for `"<task_title> <feature_id>"` and injected the results into your prompt as a `## RAG Context` block (look for it near the top of your context).
2. Appended a `rag_pre_flight` entry to the task YAML log recording what it found.

You should **read the `## RAG Context` block before doing any other work**. Do not call `mcp__rag-server__rag_query` again with the same query — the runtime has already done it. If you need to look up something specific mid-task (a different topic from the task title), invoke the `rag-context` skill explicitly; it appends a separate log entry rather than touching the runtime's `rag_pre_flight` record.

---

## Must then implement, self-review, and open the PR

After the branch is created, the `started` log entry is written, and RAG context has been injected (or skipped), proceed directly through the full execution contract **without pausing for human confirmation**:

### Step 1 — Implement

Read the following documents **in order** before writing any code:

1. `docs/features/<feature_id>/product-spec.md` — understand the original user requirements and business constraints
2. `docs/features/<feature_id>/technical-design.md` — understand the implementation approach
3. `tasks.md` (under `## T<n> — <title>`) — understand the specific task scope and subtasks

Make all required code and documentation changes in the implementation repo. Commit incrementally as logical units. Push each commit to the feature branch.

Update `task.execution.last_updated_by` and `task.execution.last_updated_at` in the task YAML as work progresses.

#### Format before every commit

Before running `git commit`, always run the project's format command to ensure committed code is properly formatted. Detect the formatter from the project:

- If `package.json` has a `format` script → `yarn format` or `npm run format`
- If `package.json` has a `lint:fix` or `eslint` script → `yarn lint:fix` or `npm run lint:fix`
- If `Makefile` has a `fmt` or `format` target → `make fmt` or `make format`
- If the repo is Go → `gofmt -w .`
- If the repo is Python and has a `pyproject.toml` or `.ruff.toml` → `ruff format .`; otherwise `black .`

Invoke `pr-self-review` on the completed branch. Fix any blocking issues found. Re-commit and re-push. Repeat until no blocking issues remain.

### Step 3 — Execute the test plan

Read the test plan from the PR description template or from `tasks.md` under `## T<n>`. Execute every item in the test plan:

- For items that can be run (compile checks, unit tests, linters): run them and record actual output.
- For items that require code inspection (config file verification, logic traces): read the relevant files and verify each claim explicitly.
- If a test plan item fails: fix the issue, re-commit, re-push, then re-run the full test plan from scratch.
- **Hard stop** if a test plan item cannot be made to pass after 3 attempts — set `status: blocked`, write `blocked_reason`, append a log entry, and stop. Do not open a PR for failing tests.

After all items pass, record the results (pass/fail per item, test suite counts if applicable) to post as a PR comment in Step 4.

### Step 4 — Create PR

Invoke `pr-create` to push the final branch state and open the pull request. The task status will be set to `in_review` by `pr-create`. Immediately after the PR is created, post the test plan results as a comment on the PR.

### Autonomous execution rules

- Do not ask for confirmation between steps.
- Do not stop after branch setup and wait.
- If a blocking issue arises during implementation that cannot be resolved (ambiguous spec, missing dependency, repeated test failure after 3 attempts), follow the **blocking exit sequence** below and exit — do not open a PR for broken work.

**Blocking exit sequence:**
1. Commit any partial work on the **implementation repo** task branch:
   ```
   git add -A && git commit -m "wip: partial work before block — <brief summary>"
   git push origin feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   ```
   If there is nothing to commit (no changes since last commit), skip the commit but still push to ensure the branch is current on remote.
2. Capture the WIP SHA from the implementation repo:
   ```
   git rev-parse HEAD
   ```
3. Write `blocked_context` to the task YAML:
   ```yaml
   blocked_context:
     wip_branch: feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
     wip_sha: <SHA from step 2>
     pushed_at: <ISO 8601 timestamp via date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z>
   ```
4. Set `status: blocked`, write `blocked_reason` and `suggested_next_step`, append a `blocked` log entry with a real local timestamp.
5. Commit and push the updated task YAML to the **management repo** task branch.

- All four steps (implement → self-review → test plan → PR) are part of a single `/start-implementation` invocation.

---

## Re-do mode

Triggered when the task status is `in_review` and the PR has been rejected or has review comments to address.

### When to use

Use re-do mode instead of the normal flow when:
- the task status is `in_review` (not `ready`)
- the user explicitly asks to fix review comments or re-do the task

### Must verify (re-do)

- task file exists
- task status is `in_review`
- task has a PR field with a valid PR reference
- repo local path resolves correctly

### Must then (re-do)

1. **Update the branch** — fetch remote state first, then check out and fast-forward the feature branch:
   ```
   git fetch origin
   git checkout feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   git reset --hard origin/feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   ```
   **Hard stop** if any of these commands fail (e.g. branch does not exist on remote) — append a log entry to the task file (action: `blocked`, note: the git error message) and stop. Do not proceed.

2. **Check existing changes** — review what is already on the branch vs the repo's base branch (resolved from `workspace.yaml -> repos[].base_branch` for the task's repo):
   ```
   git diff <base_branch>...HEAD --stat
   git log <base_branch>..HEAD --oneline
   ```

3. **Fetch PR review comments** — retrieve all review comments from the PR using the GitHub API with `GITHUB_TOKEN` from project `.env`:
   ```
   GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments
   GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews
   ```
   Read and understand every comment before making any changes.

4. **Fix the comments** — apply all required changes to resolve the review feedback.

5. **Format and commit** — run the project's format command (see "Format before every commit" rule above), stage any formatter changes, then commit and push:
   ```
   git add <changed files>
   git commit -m "fix: address PR review comments (<summary>)"
   git push origin feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   ```

6. **Mark in_review again** — update the task log with the fix action and ensure status remains `in_review`.

### Must append task log (re-do)

- action: fixed review comments
- PR comments addressed (brief summary)
- actor: resolved `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`
- timestamp: real local time via `date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z` — never hardcode

---

## Blocked recovery mode

Triggered when task `status === "ready"` AND `task.blocked_context` is non-null. Use this mode instead of normal branch setup when **both** conditions are true.

### When to use

- task status is `ready`
- `task.blocked_context` is non-null (a prior run committed partial WIP work)

### Must then (recovery)

1. **Fetch origin on both repos**:
   ```
   git fetch origin   # run on both implementation repo and management repo
   ```

2. **Management repo — checkout the WIP branch**:
   ```
   git checkout <blocked_context.wip_branch>
   git reset --hard origin/<blocked_context.wip_branch>
   ```
   **Hard stop** if either command fails — set `status: blocked`, append a log entry, and stop.

3. **Implementation repo — checkout the same WIP branch**:
   ```
   git checkout <blocked_context.wip_branch>
   git reset --hard origin/<blocked_context.wip_branch>
   ```
   **Hard stop** if either command fails — set `status: blocked`, append a log entry, and stop.

4. **Read prior context** — read `blocked_reason` and `suggested_next_step` from the task YAML to understand why the prior run stopped. Use this as additional context before continuing implementation.

5. **Append a `recovery_started` log entry** to the task YAML with a real local timestamp. Commit and push this to the management repo task branch.

6. **Proceed with implementation** — continue from where the prior run left off. The partial WIP commits are already on the branch.

7. **On successful PR creation** — set `blocked_context: null` in the task YAML, commit the change, and push to the task branch before the PR is opened.

2. `docs/features/<feature_id>/technical-design.md` — understand the implementation approach
3. `tasks.md` (under `## T<n> — <title>`) — understand the specific task scope and subtasks

Make all required code and documentation changes in the implementation repo. Commit incrementally as logical units. Push each commit to the feature branch.

Update `task.execution.last_updated_by` and `task.execution.last_updated_at` in the task YAML as work progresses.

#### Format before every commit

Before running `git commit`, always run the project's format command to ensure committed code is properly formatted. Detect the formatter from the project:

- If `package.json` has a `format` script → `yarn format` or `npm run format`
- If `package.json` has a `lint:fix` or `eslint` script → `yarn lint:fix` or `npm run lint:fix`
- If `Makefile` has a `fmt` or `format` target → `make fmt` or `make format`
- If the repo is Go → `gofmt -w .`
- If the repo is Python and has a `pyproject.toml` or `.ruff.toml` → `ruff format .`; otherwise `black .`

### Step 2 — Self-review

Invoke `pr-self-review` on the completed branch. Fix any blocking issues found. Re-commit and re-push. Repeat until no blocking issues remain.

### Step 3 — Execute the test plan

Read the test plan from the PR description template or from `tasks.md` under `## T<n>`. Execute every item in the test plan:

- For items that can be run (compile checks, unit tests, linters): run them and record actual output.
- For items that require code inspection (config file verification, logic traces): read the relevant files and verify each claim explicitly.
- If a test plan item fails: fix the issue, re-commit, re-push, then re-run the full test plan from scratch.
- **Default (interactive)**: **Hard stop** if a test plan item cannot be made to pass after 3 attempts — set `status: blocked`, write `blocked_reason`, append a log entry, and stop. Do not open a PR for failing tests.
- **Agent-runtime variant** (`CLAUDE_AGENT_RUNTIME=1`): if a test plan item cannot be made to pass after 3 attempts, do **not** hard-stop before opening a PR. After all items pass (or after 3 failed attempts in agent-runtime mode), record the results (pass/fail per item, test suite counts if applicable) to post as a PR comment in Step 4.

Invoke `pr-create` to push the final branch state and open the pull request. Immediately after the PR is created, post the test plan results as a comment on the PR.

**Default (interactive)**: `pr-create` sets the task status to `in_review` in the management repo.

**Agent-runtime variant** (`CLAUDE_AGENT_RUNTIME=1`): invoke `/pr-create` as normal to push the branch and create the GitHub PR. - Do not ask for confirmation between steps.
- Do not stop after branch setup and wait.

## Re-do mode

Triggered when the task status is `in_review` and the PR has been rejected or has review comments to address.

### When to use

Use re-do mode instead of the normal flow when:
- the task status is `in_review` (not `ready`)
- the user explicitly asks to fix review comments or re-do the task

### Must verify (re-do)

- task file exists
- task status is `in_review`
- task has a PR field with a valid PR reference
- repo local path resolves correctly

### Must then (re-do)

1. **Update the branch** — fetch remote state first, then check out and fast-forward the feature branch:

   git checkout feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   git reset --hard origin/feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   ```

4. **Fix the comments** — apply all required changes to resolve the review feedback.

5. **Format and commit** — run the project's format command (see "Format before every commit" rule above), stage any formatter changes, then commit and push:

   git push origin feature/<feature_id>-<work_id>
   ```

- actor: resolved `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`

2	 * Briefing generator for the Claude executor.
3	 *
4	 * Produces a markdown briefing written to a temporary file before the executor
5	 * process is spawned. The briefing carries only task-specific context — it does
6	 * not contain workflow-protocol rules (those are the orchestrator's concern).
7	 *
8	 * The briefing instructs Claude to invoke /start-implementation, which handles
9	 * the full execution contract: implement → self-review → test plan → PR → post
10	 * comment → write result.json. The CLAUDE_AGENT_RUNTIME=1 env var triggers the
11	 * agent-runtime variant of the skill (skip task YAML mutations, write result.json).
12	 */
13	
14	import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
15	import { join } from "node:path";
16	import {
17	  preambleSection,
18	  identitySection,
19	  taskContextSection,
20	  modelSection,
21	  joinSections,
22	} from "./briefing-template.js";

24	export interface BriefingOpts {
25	  taskId: string;

27	  taskTitle: string;

39	 * Generate the per-activation briefing markdown for the Claude executor.
40	 *
41	 * Sections (in order):
42	 *   0. Continuing previous run (Layer 3) — prepended only when handover.md exists
43	 *   1. Preamble — automated context, no interactive session
44	 *   2. ## Identity
45	 *   3. ## Your assigned task
46	 *   4. ## What you must do
47	 *   5. ## Model
48	 *   6. ## Rules
49	 *   7. ## Checkpoint discipline (Layer 2)
50	 */
51	export function generateBriefing(opts: BriefingOpts): string {
52	  const {
53	    taskId,
54	    featureId,
55	    taskTitle,
56	    taskBranch,
57	    taskRepo,
58	    taskRepoRoot,
59	    workspaceRoot,

61	    gitAuthorName,

66	  // ── Layer 3: prepend handover.md from previous run if present ────────────────
67	  const handoverSection = readHandoverSection(taskRepoRoot, taskBranch);
68	
69	  const coreSections = joinSections(
70	    preambleSection(),
71	    identitySection({ gitAuthorEmail, gitAuthorName }),
72	    taskContextSection("Your assigned task", {
73	      taskId, featureId, taskTitle, taskBranch,

75	    }),

84	      "",

86	    ],
87	    modelSection(implementationModel),
88	    [

123	    "declare the work complete, perform a graceful checkpoint:",

132	    "5. Exit cleanly.",
133	    "",

135	    "you exit without writing a result file — but a graceful checkpoint you write is",
136	    "richer and more useful for the next agent.",

138	}

141	
142	/**
143	 * Read handover.md from the task working directory if present.
144	 * Returns the formatted section string, or undefined if no handover exists.
145	 */
146	function readHandoverSection(taskRepoRoot: string, taskBranch: string): string | undefined {
147	  const handoverPath = join(taskRepoRoot, "handover.md");
148	  if (!existsSync(handoverPath)) return undefined;
149	
150	  try {

152	    if (!content) return undefined;
153	    return `## Continuing previous run\n\n${content}`;
154	  } catch {
155	    return undefined;
156	  }
